evidence_spans.claim: The proposed optimized CNN achieved 81.56% accuracy, exceeding prior approaches tested only on ABIDE I.

evidence_spans.text:
The ABIDE-I dataset is 
composed of 1112 resting-state functional magnetic resonance 
imaging (rs-fMRI) datasets. Among these, 573 datasets belong 
to typically developing persons, while 539 datasets belong to 
individuals with autism. On the other hand, the ABIDE-II 
dataset consists of 1014 resting-state functional magnetic 
resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) datasets. Out of these, 521 
datasets are from individuals with autism, and 593 datasets are 
from typically developing control individuals.
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE-I has 1112 datasets (573 TC, 539 ASD); ABIDE-II has 1014 (should be 1114 per abstract) with 521 ASD and 593 control datasets.

assessments.support: Diagnosis source/instrument is never stated; labels appear to be taken directly from ABIDE group assignment ('Each image was manually labelled and assigned a group') with no mention of ADOS/ADI-R or inclusion/exclusion criteria beyond 'resources and age'.

No preprocessing pipeline (e.g. CPAC/DPARSF), connectivity feature extraction, or atlas/parcellation is described; the paper refers only to 'images' and 'heat maps' fed to CNN/transfer-learning models with no stated derivation from raw rs-fMRI.
Outcome is binary ASD vs control classification, but how group labels were sourced/validated is not reported.

No train/test split ratio, cross-validation scheme, or held-out evaluation is reported for the authors' own experiments; results are reported per 'resource' (site) as separate subsets rather than leave-site-out; no measure of uncertainty (CI) is given around the single reported accuracy figures.

risk_of_bias.summary: Predictive classification study with no reported preprocessing/atlas, no reported train/test or cross-validation protocol, no leakage control statement, and no diagnosis-source documentation; accuracy figures are reported as single point estimates without uncertainty.

charting.title: Analysis of Brain Imaging Data for the Detection of Early Age Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Transfer Learning Approaches for Internet of Things
charting.primary_goal: Early-age ASD detection using CNN and transfer learning on ABIDE rs-fMRI-derived images
charting.dataset_openly_available: No statement of code or participant-list release
charting.feature_types: image-based (MRI scan images / heat maps), no stated connectivity feature extraction
charting.validation_methodology: Not reported (no train/test split ratio or cross-validation scheme described); results reported per site/resource subset
charting.key_performance_results: ABIDE-I complete: CNN 78.5% acc (DTL-NN 80%); ABIDE-II complete: CNN 80.5% acc (DTL-NN 83%); ABIDE-I+II complete: CNN 81.56% acc, DTL-NN 82.31% acc
charting.summary_key_findings: An optimized CNN and a transfer-learning (DTL-NN) model classify ASD vs control from ABIDE rs-fMRI-derived images, reaching 81.56% (CNN) and 82.31% (DTL-NN) accuracy on the combined ABIDE-I+II dataset.
charting.future_directions_recommended: Development of an assistive tool for individuals with autism to improve daily well-being and efficiency.
charting.reviewer_notes: No preprocessing pipeline, atlas, train/test split, or diagnosis-instrument information reported; total N and per-site tables are internally inconsistent (abstract says ABIDE-II = 1114 datasets vs Table II = 1014).

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (CNN and transfer learning); ABIDE-I (1112 datasets: 539 ASD, 573 TC) and ABIDE-II (reported as 1114 or 1014 datasets: 521 ASD, 593 TC) across 17 sites; combined ABIDE-I+II analysis also reported.
narrative_row.methods: MRI-derived images/heat maps from ABIDE rs-fMRI data are classified with an optimized CNN and a transfer-learning model (DTL-NN); results reported separately per data-collection site/resource and per age-based subgroup, with no described preprocessing pipeline, atlas, or train/test split.
narrative_row.outcomes: Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and F1-score reported per site and per dataset grouping; best combined ABIDE-I+II result: CNN 81.56% accuracy, DTL-NN 82.31% accuracy.
narrative_row.key_limitations: Authors note limitations from multi-site data collection (17 sites) and picture data availability (851 subjects); no cross-validation/held-out evaluation, no diagnosis-source documentation, no preprocessing/atlas details, inconsistent N reporting between abstract and tables.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Uses ABIDE I and II for diagnostic prediction but with minimal methodological transparency on cohort construction, QC, pipeline, and validation — illustrates reconstructibility and rigor gaps relevant to the dataset-publication link.

kg_link.finding: An optimized CNN and a transfer-learning model (DTL-NN) classify ASD vs control from ABIDE rs-fMRI-derived images, achieving 81.56% (CNN) and 82.31% (DTL-NN) accuracy on the combined ABIDE-I+II dataset, with no reported cross-validation or held-out-site evaluation.
